recall.minute: Encoder–decoder RNNs compress the input into one context vector, which fails on long inputs. Attention keeps all encoder states and builds a new context at each decoder step: scores e_i = score(q, k_i), weights α = softmax(e), context c = Σ α_i v_i. Scores can be dot products (fast), scaled dot products qᵀk/√d_k (the Transformer default, because Var(qᵀk) = d_k), additive vᵀtanh(W_q q + W_k k) as in Bahdanau's 2014 translation model, or multiplicative qᵀWk. Self-attention uses Q, K, V from one sequence, cross-attention queries another sequence, causal masks add −∞ to future positions for generation, and multi-head attention concatenates h heads and projects with W_O. Self-attention has O(1) path length and full parallelism at O(n²d) cost, but is permutation-equivariant, so positional encodings (learned or sinusoidal, where PE(pos + k) is a rotation of PE(pos)) are added.
